Enter the energy price per kWh. If you know the price before taxes, enter it here and use Taxes to add the applicable percentage. If your price already includes all taxes, leave Taxes at 0 %.\n\nAvoid simply dividing your total bill by the kWh used: the bill may include capacity charges, meter rental and other fixed costs unrelated to a particular print.
The effective percentage added to the electricity price. If your bill applies several taxes in succession, you can combine them into a single effective percentage.

If a bill applies 5.11269632 % electricity tax followed by 21 % VAT, the percentages are not simply added.

Effective percentage:
(1.0511269632 × 1.21 − 1) × 100
≈ 27.1864 %

A base price of €0.122/kWh would become approximately €0.1552/kWh after those taxes.

Always check the percentages on your own bill: they can change. This is a calculation example, not tax advice.
Approximate power consumed while the printer initially heats up. Estimate it using printer specifications, a power meter or a smart plug.
Approximate time spent heating up before printing. This time and the heating power determine the warm-up energy, which is added to the printing energy.
An hourly allowance for printer wear, maintenance and depreciation. It is added after the sale multiplier and is not part of the cost being multiplied.
Multiplies the piece cost (material + electricity) to obtain the main part of the selling price. Machine cost is added afterwards.\n\nPrice = Piece cost × Multiplier + Machine cost

Set up your actual costs for estimates tailored to your printer and filaments.
Enter your electricity tariff details. MakerTally will use them to calculate the energy cost of each print.
How do I calculate this percentage?

Effective taxes represent the actual increase that taxes and charges add to the base electricity price.

((Final price ÷ Base price) − 1) × 100

If your tariff already gives the final price per kWh including all taxes, you can enter that price and leave taxes at 0 %.
During initial warm-up, the printer may use more power for a short time.\n\nThese values are optional and help refine the electricity cost estimate.

If you cannot measure these values, you can leave them at 0 or use this starting reference:

1200 W for 1 minute

This is only an illustrative example. Actual consumption depends on each printer.
The cost associated with using the printer: wear, maintenance, replacement parts or depreciation.
If you do not want to include this cost, you can use €0/h.\n\nIf you are unsure what to enter, €0.25/h can serve as a starting reference.
Applied to the piece cost to obtain a suggested selling price. Machine cost is added afterwards.
The multiplier depends on your own costs and how you want to set your selling price.
Enter a valid multiplier of at least ×1
MakerTally now knows your general costs.\n\nNext, set up the filaments you use.
You will find a generic PLA example with a 1000 g spool priced at €14.99. You can edit it, delete it or create your own profiles.
We have added an example profile to help you get started.
You can edit this profile, delete it or use + to add the filaments you normally use.
The approximate electrical power used by the printer while printing with this material.

Power use can vary by filament because some materials need higher hotend or heated-bed temperatures. For example, ASA and ABS usually print at higher temperatures than PLA and may increase electricity consumption.

If you cannot measure your printer’s consumption, you can use these starting references:

PLA: 120 W
PETG: 140 W
ASA, ABS and high-temperature materials: 180 W
These are approximate reference values. Actual measurements from your printer will give more accurate estimates.
